seo.title: La Scalinatella: Family-Owned Capri Honeymoon Review 2026
seo.description: Quiet family-owned Capri Town boutique with sea views. Score 78/100, from $700/night. Verdict, suite pick, 7-night itinerary.

content.verdict: La Scalinatella (literally “the little staircase”) is the under-the-radar family-owned alternative to Capri Town’s big-name hotels — a 32-room property tucked into a quiet bougainvillea-covered hillside on via Tragara, a 6-minute walk from the Piazzetta, run by the Morgano family since 1965 (the same family that owns the historic Quisisana 200m away) and operated with a distinctly more intimate, less-frequented atmosphere than its grander sister. The property is the original 18th-century private villa “La Casetta”, expanded over the decades with adjoining gardens and a small number of cliff-edge additions, with the result that almost every room has a private terrace overlooking either the Faraglioni rocks or the Marina Piccola cove below. Two saltwater pools (one at the lower garden level, more peaceful; one upper terrace pool, more social), a single restaurant on the panoramic terrace serving Mediterranean classics (no Michelin star — the food is solid family-Italian rather than fine-dining), and a small spa with three treatment rooms. The defining experience is the cliff-edge private terraces — the property’s architectural quirk is that almost no two rooms have the same layout, and many guests develop loyalty to specific rooms (room 401 with its 270° wraparound terrace is the cult favourite). The Morgano family operates the property with a warmth that the larger Quisisana down the road cannot match — guests are greeted by name, the staff remembers preferences year to year, and the operation feels closer to a private villa stay than a hotel. The honeymoon move is a Deluxe Junior Suite with private cliff terrace, or the spectacular Royal Suite with its private pool. The defining moment: breakfast on your private terrace with the Faraglioni rocks visible through the bougainvillea and Capri Town just waking up below. Caveats: no Michelin restaurant on-site — for fine dining you walk 6 minutes to L’Olivo at Capri Palace by taxi (15 min) or eat in Capri Town; the 4-star classification reflects a more modest amenity level than the 5-star Capri Palace or J.K. Place; and the hotel is genuinely quiet — not the buzzy social scene of Quisisana 200m away. But for honeymooners who specifically want Capri Town address, intimate family-owned operation, and a private cliff terrace at a 30% lower price than the J.K. Place or Capri Palace, La Scalinatella is the secret pick.
content.best_room: A Deluxe Junior Suite with private cliff terrace facing the Faraglioni. Room 401 (270° wraparound terrace) is the cult favourite if available. For the absolute pinnacle, the Royal Suite with its private pool. Avoid the rear interior rooms without sea view.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Capri Town arrival
itinerary_7_nights.description: Sorrento hydrofoil to Marina Grande. Funicular to Piazzetta. 6-min walk to the hotel. Welcome Spumante in your cliff-edge suite. Aperitivo at the pool. Dinner at the hotel restaurant.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Around the island by boat
itinerary_7_nights.description: Private gozzo boat — Blue Grotto, Faraglioni arch, lunch at Lido del Faro. Return for siesta. Dinner at Aurora in Capri Town (the famous Pucci family restaurant).

itinerary_7_nights.title: Da Paolino lunch
itinerary_7_nights.description: Taxi down to Da Paolino (10 min) for lemon-tree lunch. Up to Capri Town. Afternoon shopping via Camerelle. Aperitivo at the Quisisana bar. Dinner at La Capannina.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Villa Jovis and Belvedere
itinerary_7_nights.description: Early walk to Villa Jovis (40 min from hotel). Lunch at the Belvedere di Tragara overlook. Afternoon at the pool. Dinner at the hotel restaurant.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Anacapri day
itinerary_7_nights.description: Taxi to Anacapri (15 min). Chairlift to Monte Solaro. Lunch at Da Gelsomina. Villa San Michele. Dinner at L’Olivo (2 Michelin stars) at Capri Palace.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Da Luigi at the Faraglioni
itinerary_7_nights.description: Walk down via Tragara to the Da Luigi shuttle. Sunbeds and lunch at Da Luigi ai Faraglioni. Afternoon swim. Aperitivo at the hotel. Final dinner at Aurora.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Slow departure
itinerary_7_nights.description: Final breakfast on your terrace. Walk to the Piazzetta. Funicular down to Marina Grande.

caveats: No on-site Michelin restaurant — the food is family-Italian solid rather than fine dining.
4-star classification reflects a more modest amenity level than Capri Palace or J.K. Place.
Genuinely quiet — not the social buzz of Quisisana 200m away.

faqs.question: Good for honeymooners?
faqs.answer: Excellent for couples wanting Capri Town address, intimate family-owned operation, and private cliff terraces at 30% lower price than the 5-star competition.

faqs.question: Best time to visit?
faqs.answer: May, June, September, October. Closed November to mid-April.

faqs.question: Book in advance?
faqs.answer: Deluxe Junior Suites and Royal Suite 6–9 months for May–September. Standard rooms 4 months. Repeat guests have first refusal on specific rooms.

faqs.question: Adults-only?
faqs.answer: No, but the intimate scale and family-owned atmosphere means families are uncommon. Atmosphere is adult and quiet.

faqs.question: Best room type?
faqs.answer: Deluxe Junior Suite with private cliff terrace. Room 401 the cult favourite. Royal Suite the pinnacle.

faqs.question: How to get there?
faqs.answer: Naples (NAP). Sorrento hydrofoil to Marina Grande (25 min). Funicular to Piazzetta (4 min). 6-min walk.
